notes.430: Code, not text: Arabic-Indic digit range in toLatin() regex. Left unchanged on purpose (digits, not letters) so customers typing Arabic digits still work. Same for 431, 432, 433.

notes.433: Code: Persian digit lookup string. Left unchanged on purpose (see 430).
notes.437: Followed by Intl.DateTimeFormat(ar-SA-u-ca-gregory-nu-latn): the locale must be switched to an English one (e.g. en-GB) in code, or dates stay in Arabic. Same for the date in 448. Also 531 does dayLabel(...).replace(“يوصل ”, “”) which becomes replace(“Arrives ”, “”) after global replacement, so keep 437 exactly “Arrives”.
notes.438: Key comparison it.g === “Supplies” (also 440 includes(“plant”), 456 it.g === “Greenery”). Works only if catalog.json / the item data is translated with the same strings.
notes.446: uPlural uses Arabic plural rules (plural only for 3–10). For English the code should use the plural for any n !== 1, otherwise you get “11 stem”, “2 stem”.
notes.452: Value is “per ” WITH a trailing space: in the source the unit name follows with no space, so it must read “per stem”. Do not strip.
notes.454: Same Arabic word is used after a list count here (needs “items”) and for n === 1 in 513 (needs “item”). Translated as “item”; the count at 454 needs a plural in code.
notes.480: Sentence is category name + this + optional “ from origin” + “.”, giving e.g. “Spray rose — natural, sold wholesale from Kenya.” English word order forced the dash construction.
notes.802: Regex keywords (802–804, 806–823, 905–907) use [Xx] character classes instead of plain lowercase: these regexes have no i flag and are tested against raw product names (Arabic kw contains hamza letters, so it is not run through norm()), which are capitalized in English, e.g. “White Hydrangea Bouquet”. Other alternatives in the same SHADES regexes come from other chunks.
notes.905: CATS filter /…/.test(p.name) runs on the raw, capitalized English name, so [Hh]ydrangea, [Ll]il(y|ies), [Ss]unflower are needed or these categories come out empty.
notes.908: Arabic normalization in norm() (908–914). Written as JS \u escapes so the code behaves exactly as before with no Arabic letters in the file. Insert literally: if the replacement step uses Python re.sub with a string replacement, the \u will error, so use plain string replacement.
notes.917: split(“،”) on product spec; now split(“,”) since English specs use commas. shortSpec then shows the first ingredient.
notes.929: Used after a count (number of bouquets), so plural “bouquets”. Same for 945 “products”.
notes.935: Followed by an RTL arrow ← in the source; for English it should be → (code/markup change).
notes.1031: Regex /^Payment: .*$/m must match the message line built with 992 “Payment:”. Keep 992 and 1031 in sync.
notes.1046: Builds “Order within 3 h 20 min for delivery today” from 1045 + hours + 1046 + minutes + 1047.
